rationale: Gives the follower-side lead its own account so that the run does not end with a question that nothing answers. The account states what the source establishes and what it does not: the follower's Promise builds its LogSync from the leader's numbers, and for a NoSnapshot entry type the prefix it hands to its own storage reaches get_suffix, whose subtraction of the trimmed index is unguarded, while the snapshot-capable type takes the Complete-snapshot branch instead. What is not established is reachability: it needs a leader whose Prepare reports a decided or accepted index below a follower's compacted index, which in turn needs a history in which that follower learned something the newly elected leader missed - legal in principle, never driven in this harness, and not something a source reading alone can settle either way, because it depends on which of the two branches the follower takes and on how compaction and elections interleave. The account therefore records the mechanism, the exact conditions and the probe that would decide it, and keeps the defect claim unresolved rather than asserting an abort that no run has produced. No other record changed and no execution was requested; the run's other five questions keep their current accounts.

interpretations.rationale: The mechanism is sourced and the reachability is not. Sourced: the follower's handle_prepare builds its Promise's LogSync from the leader's Prepare rather than from its own log - create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx) when the follower's accepted round is greater than the leader's, and create_log_sync(prep.accepted_idx, prep.decided_idx) when the rounds are equal and the follower's accepted index is greater (follower.rs 13-51) - and create_log_sync reads the created suffix from the follower's own storage at that prefix (mod.rs 405-432). For an entry type whose Snapshot is NoSnapshot that read is get_suffix, and the shipped in-memory storage subtracts its trimmed index from the requested one without a guard, which the storage-level probe in this run showed aborting below the trimmed index (receipt 9daa1fc530244c7ea0863a1d73d90960 events 0 and 1, with the process naming memory_storage.rs:103). For the snapshot-capable type the same call takes the snapshot branch whenever the follower's own decided index exceeds the prefix - which it does here, since the prefix is below the follower's compacted index - and builds a Complete snapshot instead, so the two entry types are expected to differ exactly as they did in that probe. Not established: whether such a prefix is ever handed over inside a cluster. It requires a Prepare whose decided or accepted index lies below the follower's compacted index, hence a leader that reports less than a follower holds, hence a history in which the follower learned a decision or an accept round that the newly elected leader missed; that is legal in principle - the follower's compacted index is bounded only by its own decided index, not by anyone else's - but no execution drove it, and a source reading cannot decide it either way because it depends on the interleaving of election, compaction and prepare handling rather than on a single guard. The probe that would settle it is named in the discriminator: a three-node NoSnapshot cluster in which a lagging node wins the election after another leader decided and the followers compacted, sampling both the numbers in the Prepare and whether the follower's Promise is built and sent, then the same shape with the snapshot-capable entry type as the control. Until that runs, this account asserts no abort.
counterevidence: The storage-level probe's abort is not evidence for this path: it showed a direct caller below the trimmed index aborting, which is the mechanism this lead would use, but it said nothing about whether the follower's Promise ever supplies such a prefix.

The observed drift lineage never produced the precondition: in every receipt the leader's decided index was the greatest in the cluster when it sent a Prepare, so the follower's branch always passed a prefix at or above the follower's content, which is why this lead stayed unseen across twelve experiments.
The snapshot-capable entry type cannot show the abort even if the prefix is below the follower's compacted index, so a negative result with that type would not dispose of the NoSnapshot case.
limitations: Reachability is argued from what is legal rather than from a driven history: the harness has produced a lagging leader before, but never one that prepared a follower which had compacted above the leader's own decided index.

Both branches of the follower's LogSync construction share the hazard only in the non-snapshot storage path; the snapshot branch's own bound and the receiving side's sync_log were not re-read line by line for this account, so a second protection may exist there.

The account rests on the same three-node, in-memory, no-persistence configuration as the rest of the run; a deployment where compaction and elections interleave differently could reach or miss the precondition.
No panic was observed, so the defect claim is unresolved by construction: the account records a hypothesis with its conditions, not a finding.
interpretations.joint_history: This question was opened from the same lineage as the trim child's storage-ledger work: the follower-side read it points at is the same storage call the storage-level probe measured in receipt 9daa1fc530244c7ea0863a1d73d90960, whose experiment (116b57435bab466d86666432432b5ee5-experiment) belongs to the trim investigation, and the compaction bounds it depends on are the ones the trim and snapshot children established (receipts ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a and e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c). The receipt is cited here for the storage call only, read on its own samples, and no measurement is combined across investigations.
